external_specification.provider: SQLite public language specification and independently executable sqlite3 engine
relevant_semantics: an inner join considers left-right row combinations
the ON predicate retains exactly the row pairs for which the expression is true
duplicate join keys retain row-pair bag multiplicity

oracle.engine: Python standard-library sqlite3 linked to an external SQLite implementation
ddl: CREATE TABLE a(row_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, join_key INTEGER NOT NULL)
CREATE TABLE b(row_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, join_key INTEGER NOT NULL)
oracle.query: SELECT a.row_id, b.row_id FROM a INNER JOIN b ON a.join_key = b.join_key ORDER BY a.row_id ASC, b.row_id ASC
oracle.second_route_independent_crosscheck: sorted Python comprehension over integer key equality

declared_domain.row_id: unique within each side, non-bool unsigned 32-bit integer
declared_domain.key_multiplicity: duplicate keys are permitted on either side
declared_domain.input_sides: A and B are both nonempty
declared_domain.capacity: number of unique output id-pairs does not exceed the sealed semantic capacity

mapping.row_mapping: (row_id,k) maps to binary32 AABB [k,0,k+1,1] carrying row_id
mapping.why_exact: k and k+1 are integers no greater than 2^24 and are exactly representable in binary32; threshold area >= 1.0 is therefore true exactly when the integer keys are equal

keys 42 and 43 do not join even though their closed unit boxes touch at a boundary
keys 0 and 16777215 match exactly at both ends of the admitted key domain
an A key absent from B produces no row
